an10.39:1.1: Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him:
an10.39:1.2: “Bhante, it is said: ‘Schism in the Saṅgha, schism in the Saṅgha.’
an10.39:1.3: How is there schism in the Saṅgha?”
an10.39:1.4: “Here, Ānanda, (1) bhikkhus explain non-Dhamma as Dhamma … as in AN10.37 …
an10.39:1.5: and (10) what has been prescribed by the Tathāgata as not having been prescribed by him.
an10.39:1.6: On these ten grounds they withdraw and go apart. They perform legal acts separately and recite the Pātimokkha separately.
an10.39:1.7: It is in this way, Ānanda, that there is schism in the Saṅgha.”
an10.39:2.1: “But, Bhante, when one causes schism in a harmonious Saṅgha, what does one generate?”
an10.39:2.2: “One generates evil lasting for an eon, Ānanda.”
an10.39:2.3: “But, Bhante, what is that evil lasting for an eon?”
an10.39:2.4: “One is tormented in hell for an eon, Ānanda.”
an10.39:3.1: One who causes schism in the Saṅgha is bound for misery, bound for hell, to abide there for an eon.
an10.39:3.3: Delighting in factions, established in non-Dhamma,
an10.39:3.4: he falls away from security from bondage.
an10.39:3.5: Having caused schism in a harmonious Saṅgha,
an10.39:3.6: he is tormented in hell for an eon.
